newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-EU clears 23.76 bln francs aid for GAN.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EU clears 23.76 bln francs aid for GAN.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday cleared a French rescue plan for GAN, the country's fifth largest insurer, after the French government confirmed it would privatise the loss-making firm.

The plan includes a capital injection of 11 billion francs ($1.77 billion), mainly to cover huge losses recorded by GAN's property unit UIC, a state guarantee valued at 9.9 billion francs for future losses in restructuring the GAN group and a 2.86-billion-franc state injection carried out in 1995.
It is the second time in two years that the EU has agreed to rescue plans for GAN bringing the total bill for French taxpayers to 23.76 billion francs.

In return for the new rescue plan, GAN will sell its banking unit CIC; divest property units UIC and UIS; sell other holdings for a total value of 2.4 billion francs; and halve its foreign commercial interests, the Commission said in a statement.
The Commission said these divestments must be carried out before the end of 1998.
It said the measures, some of which have already been announced by the French group, would ensure the return to profit of GAN, which has lost 35 billion francs since 1992.
"(The Commission) reached the conclusion that the new restructuring measures being undertaken will help GAN to break even or do even better," it said in a statement.
GAN said earlier this month it had started the sale of UIC which ran up 30 billion francs of losses in three years, the root of GAN's financial problems

The new French government of Socialist leader Lionel Jospin recently endorsed the planned privatisation of GAN and a number of insurance companies have said they were interested in the company including AGF and Allianz of Germany. $1 = 6.20
